## Source: amazon-inspector (3dd746168a2e733a835005f5fd321e1bab9a24688a4c5d413247ae065ea29786)
black-spindle@999.0.0 declares a `postinstall` lifecycle hook in package.json that executes `curl http://778e-181-63-25-28.ngrok-free.app/test` on every `npm install`. The destination is a short-lived, anonymous ngrok-free.app HTTPS/HTTP tunnel unrelated to any declared publisher, contacted over plain HTTP with no pinning or verification. The shipped `index.js` is an empty stub, so the manifest's lifecycle hook is the package's entire effect: installing the package causes the installer's host to contact an attacker-controlled endpoint and discloses install-time metadata (source IP, timing, user-agent) to that endpoint. The 999.0.0 version and single-line postinstall-beacon shape are consistent with dependency-confusion / install-telemetry beaconing rather than a legitimate library.

## Source: ossf-package-analysis (c5ef30c4ec24f78fa57d10f6bd8e7fb7be307fc23e833428af785b2013bf2fab)
The OpenSSF Package Analysis project identified 'black-spindle' @ 999.0.0 (npm) as malicious.

It is considered malicious because:

- The package communicates with a domain associated with malicious activity.

- The package executes one or more commands associated with malicious behavior.
